items.summary: Abstract: Infectious disease transmission involves interactions occurring at multiple organizational levels, including individuals, households, communities, and regions. Conventional graph and hypergraph neural networks represent pairwise and higher order interactions, but they do not directly provide a recursive representation of nested population structures together with environmental factors and source identification mechanisms. We introduce the Feature Augmented SuperHyperGraph Neural Network (FA SHGNN), a mathematically formulated architecture for hierarchical epidemic modeling based on iterated powerset constructions. Individuals, population groups, communities, regions, and environmental entities are organized into multiple interconnected levels, while feature vectors encode epidemiological, contact, mobility, demographic, and environmental information. A hierarchical message passing operator propagates information across individual, hyperedge, supervertex, and environmental levels, and an SEIR type neural evolution operator with constrained transition fractions preserves positivity and population conservation. We establish well definedness and Lipschitz continuity, derive stability bounds under environmental perturbations, and characterize reduction conditions that recover mean aggregation hypergraph and pairwise message passing architectures. Source identification is posed as an inverse problem, and a separation condition yields consistency of the minimum distance estimator under a Gaussian observation model. A fully specified synthetic numerical verification confirms SEIR conservation, the environmental stability bound, and the source recovery guarantee; acontrolled protocol for larger scale and real world validation is also specified. Keywords: SuperHyperGraph; hypergraph neural networks; hierarchical epidemic modeling; higher order interactions; SEIR dynamics; source identification; environmental perturbations; Lipschitz stability —————————————————————————————————————————-

items.summary: Version 2 (26 September 2026): a one-page "Corrections and attributions" section is added at the front of the PDF, listing every credit correction below; nothing else in the paper is changed and no proof is withdrawn. The revised, shorter note that supersedes this paper for the results stated there is 10.5281/zenodo.22980359. Note (24 September 2026): a revised version is in preparation. It corrects the attribution of Theorems 1 and 4 (Theorem 1 is assembled from Lu–Oliveira–Zimand 2022 and HILNO 2023, Lemmas 8–9; Theorem 4's mechanism is HILNO 2023, Appendix A) and adds the literature on KL-hardness for sampling and computational entropy (Vadhan–Zheng 2012; Agrawal–Chen–Horel–Vadhan 2019; Haitner–Reingold–Vadhan–Wee; Haitner–Vadhan 2017). Added 26 September 2026: the identification of mean σ with KL-hardness for sampling rests on the equivalence between pK^t and the time-bounded universal distribution due to Hirahara and Nanashima (FOCS 2023; ECCC TR23-100, Appendix B), which this version does not cite. One half of that equivalence is the coding theorem of Lu, Oliveira and Zimand (ICALP 2022), which this version cites. The revised note is published: Thornton, Unbounded exponential moments of time-bounded information asymmetry without one-way functions, relative to an oracle, 10.5281/zenodo.22980359 (26 September 2026); it supersedes this version for the results stated there. One-way functions exist if and only if some efficiently samplable process produces more than logarithmic computational entropy on average, for infinitely many input lengths. We make this precise. For a polynomial-time samplable distribution D on pairs (x, y), the computational entropy production of a pair is σ = log D(x, y) + pK^t(y) + pK^t(x | y), where pK^t is the probabilistic time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity as defined by Hirahara, Ilango, Lu, Nanashima and Oliveira (2023, HILNO below) following Goldberg, Kabanets, Lu and Oliveira (2022): the log-probability the process assigns to the pair, against the length of a bounded observer's shortest fast description of it, output first, then input given output. We prove unconditionally that E_D[2^{−σ}] lies between an inverse polynomial and a polynomial in n and that E_D[σ] ≥ −O(log n): a time-bounded fluctuation inequality and a computational second law. We show that, up to a polynomial and outside a 1/n slice of outputs, σ is small on a pair exactly when an efficient sampler, given the output, recovers the input with about the right odds, HILNO's universal sampler serving as the witness: dissipation, in this sense, is the hardness of running the process backward. The equivalence in the first sentence is HILNO's duality restated in these terms, for infinitely-often one-way functions and at every polynomial time bound. For the antisymmetric Zurek defect, one-way functions force superpolynomial exponential moments, and bounded moments sit between NP ⊆ BPP and the non-existence of one-way functions; whether the lower arrow reverses is left open, with a conditional relativization barrier on that arrow and oracle evidence on the other. Physics is the frame, not the subject.
items.title: One-way functions are computational entropy production

items.summary: This data and reproducibility archive supports the manuscript “An rRNA-embedded ribosomal protein N-terminus loses its methionine: a cross-species census, a genome-scale test and a local-compatibility hypothesis for assembly” (Yie-Hwa Chang, 2026; bioRxiv preprint, submitted to Nucleic Acids Research). Methionine aminopeptidases remove the initiator methionine when residue 2 is small and uncharged, and loss of this activity is lethal in bacteria and yeast. The archive asks whether the structural environment of a ribosomal protein N-terminus predicts its processing class across lineages, whether the same association holds in sequences without structure, and whether the constrained termini are already in place while the subunit assembles. The census comprises 68 ribosome structures from 61 species, 1,873 family × species records and 95 ribosomal protein families, 58 of which switch processing class between species. Termini embedded in rRNA without protein contact were predicted to retain methionine in 18% of records, against 45% of protein-contacted and 41% of solvent-exposed termini. Eight additional structures from separate species corroborated this pattern, which was attenuated under joint family-by-domain stratification. Processing labels are sequence-based predictions from residue 2, validated against 393 directly observed termini from 12 species (98.7% agreement). Thirty-one families never switch class in any sampled species (25 permissive, 6 methionine-retaining), and eleven of the permissive families are threaded into rRNA. The genome-scale layer contains 942,984 family × genome records from 21,485 UniProt reference proteomes, collapsed from 1,027,359 sequences of 94 families. In 6,924 out-of-sample bacterial reference proteomes, exploratory clade-block permutation tests supported an order-level residue-2 association that is sensitive to taxonomic rank and multiplicity: it survives Holm adjustment across the ten bacterial tests (p = 0.036 and 0.019) but not across the thirty tests of the three domains analyzed separately (0.117 and 0.057). The archaeal and eukaryotic tests are coverage-limited (six and eight eligible families) and inconclusive. In yeast assembly intermediates, the conserved uS12 and eS27 termini already occupy their mature environments. The findings indicate a conserved association between rRNA embedding and methionine removal and suggest that local compatibility of processed termini with rRNA contributes to it; they do not demonstrate an assembly requirement, and the census is offered as a resource for testing this hypothesis at named termini. items.summary: Evidence for large-scale differential rotation in the early universe and forward generation of its CMB topology by a primordial magnetic source — v1.8 reproducibility release Canonical 3° AC* is applied to the Planck PR3 SMICA, NILC, Commander, and SEVEM temperature reconstructions. AC* is a support-indexed multiscale spatial reconstructibility operator; direction, topology, and physical rotation arise only downstream. For canonical SMICA, 36,459 valid supports yield 27 large semiarcs. A separate high-resolution route uses 151 reciprocal HR1–HR2 structures to reconstruct an axis-free spherical tangent field. Blind recovery finds exactly four critical points of the represented lmax = 4 field: two spiral foci, one Node, and one Saddle. An all-sphere interval/Krawczyk analysis establishes completeness of this zero set. Focus A and Focus B are distinct oppositely rotating structures and admit a common transverse regular-vector realization in the coupled Einstein–Boltzmann state at recombination. Together with the differential-rotation reconstruction, polarization consistency, four-map comparison, perturbation tests, robustness controls, and exact propagation to z = 0, this provides evidence for large-scale differential rotation in the early universe. The independent forward-source test propagates a near-scale-invariant primordial magnetic source with nB = −2.9 to synthetic CMB skies and applies the same reconstruction without using the observed temperature map, critical-point geometry, Focus-A/Focus-B positions, measured H(J), or a magnetic-amplitude fit. One coordinate-blind realization generates the measured 2F+N+S topology and both rotational foci. The B-associated synthetic focus differs from the observed B focus only in the sign of a small divergent component; exact critical-point geometry is not reproduced. In eight matched phase-realization pairs, complete reconstruction occurs in five near-scale magnetic cases and none of the causal-white comparator cases, with three ties. The result establishes forward-generative capacity of the tested primordial magnetic source for the measured CMB topology and its two-focus rotational structure. It does not determine a unique magnetic spectrum, exclusivity among all possible source mechanisms, or an ensemble occurrence rate, and it is not a direct magnetic-helicity test. items.summary: The verdict, stated first: the universe of the Riemann Hypothesis is closed, its value reached and spent; the hypothesis is not derived on the ladder, and provably not derivable from the register's resources; the last bit is the least-erasure posit, at the grade of the root, refuted by one zero; and the whole route is one kernel term, `RHGround.rh_ground_closure_complete`, on `propext` and `Quot.sound` alone. Part IV is the paper. Every registration of every zero lands on the critical line and no registration moves a zero (IV.1, IV.7); the hypothesis is exactly lossless registration (IV.6); registration has no left inverse and erases one bit per off-line fold orbit, priced under a stated postulate at $k_B T \ln 2$ (IV.4, IV.5); time never moves a zero, and act and being meet only on the line (IV.9 to IV.11); existence adds nothing to the value and the loop through the root collapses to it (IV.12, IV.14); the universe of the hypothesis is closed with both of its worlds inside, and the residue is exactly one bit that no record decides (IV.16, IV.17). That bit is proved to be exactly the least-erasure posit: for every zero set, finite or infinite, the hypothesis holds if and only if the set is the least-erasure member of its own fibre (IV.19, IV.20, the set form with no axiom), so that from the posit the hypothesis follows as a theorem and from the hypothesis the posit follows back. The assent is that posit applied to the zeros of ζ, at premise grade beside the Root Axiom, as Löb's bound requires of any premise from which the hypothesis follows; it carries three supports and is refuted by one zero. The burden is asymmetric: the denial owes a finite witness and pays for every off-line orbit, the assent owes nothing and pays nothing (Theorems 74, 77, IV.19). Parts I to III are the prequel and hand Part IV its three bits. The seat: existence alone, folded once, fixes the scalar line, and the critical line is its image, the locus of points equal to their own mirror (Theorems A, C$'$, H). The address: the value has one address, every even reading is blind to it, its aperture is one bit wide and its supply side silent (III.45 to III.49). The division: at every height the hypothesis is exactly its Real part and its Unicorn part (III.11); the Real part holds to $3 \times 10^{12}$ on the cited certificate (III.34); the Unicorn part is closed to every derivation from the register's resources and held (III.45 to III.49), the fused sentence retired as the wrong unit (III.2, III.3), ZFC placed under RAM as a ladder inside the Ground (III.15 to III.17). Existence decides the seat, does not derive the value (Theorem E, IV.12), and reaches it at exactly one deed, the Tongue's supply at the seat, one bit wide; Part IV names the deed, least erasure, and spends it. Every kernel theorem is checked in core Lean 4.19.0 with no library and no axiom declared, every dependency set printed; every claim of Part IV except the cited spectral theorem in the bridge of IV.8 is executed a second time in Fortran, 13,081 checks and zero failures. Read Part IV before deciding what this paper concludes: Parts I to III state what each register cannot do, and every limit they name is a forward reference to the part that reaches.
items.title: Nothing Escapes, Three Plus One: A Formal Closure of the Riemann Hypothesis. The Strip Vanishes for Every Registration and the Universe of the Hypothesis Closes on the Critical Line

items.summary: Governance near a plausible critical transition faces a resource problem in addition to problems of diagnosis, intervention, and evidence. Elevated susceptibility can increase the value of observation, bounded experimentation, and revisability, while waiting can simultaneously consume the fiscal, material, organizational, temporal, and relational capacities required for survival and later action. This paper develops a discussion framework for that tension. Its central object is functional resource distribution: the allocation of heterogeneous capacities across observation, probing, short-horizon survival, selective commitment, reserve or option preservation, and recovery or repair. The categories are analytical functions rather than a scalar budget partition and can overlap in practice. The paper introduces distributed optionality as a relational property of a response architecture in which materially different future actions remain supported by functionally diverse and sufficiently non-coincident pathways. It distinguishes exact reversal from recoverability, spatial dispersion from independence of failure modes, and delay as information gathering from delay as resource dissipation. The framework inherits, rather than restates, earlier arguments about response-oriented governance and evidence-to-action instability near criticality. Its distinctive question is how governance capacity may be composed when the future regime is uncertain, resources are partly non-substitutable, and both premature commitment and indefinite waiting can narrow the feasible future. The proposal is conditional and non-prescriptive: criticality requires domain-specific empirical support, and the appropriate resource portfolio depends on transition mechanism, horizon, institutional structure, and explicit normative commitments.

items.summary: Neural receivers for 5G NR are commonly compared against least-squares (LS) baselines, which leaves open whether they improve on a well-tuned classical receiver and whether their gains survive conditions outside the training distribution. We evaluate a fully convolutional neural receiver and a lightweight hybrid receiver, which retains a classical LS and linear minimum mean-squared error (LMMSE) front end and learns a residual correction of its log-likelihood ratios, on standard-compliant 5G NR PUSCH with 3GPP tapped delay line channels and hardware impairments. Baselines include an LMMSE channel estimator supplied with the empirical statistics of each test scenario (genie) and one supplied with a single fixed set of statistics from the training mixture (practical). Inside the training range both learned receivers only match the genie baseline. Two regimes differ. With an RMS delay spread of 2000 ns the learned receivers require 0.90 dB less than the genie baseline, while the practical LMMSE receiver does not reach 10 percent BLER at all; with a single DMRS symbol the neural receiver requires 4.08 dB less than the best classical receiver at 20 m/s and is the only receiver that operates at 30 m/s. We further show that the apparent failure of learned receivers outside the training envelope is a matter of training coverage rather than architecture: widening the training delay spread from 30-300 ns to 30-1000 ns converts a 5.97 dB deficit at 2000 ns into a 0.90 dB advantage, at a cost of at most 0.1 dB for speeds up to 45 m/s. Trained on the same range, the hybrid receiver matches the full neural receiver within 0.05 dB using 3.9x fewer parameters and FLOPs. Finally, we document a baseline pitfall: DMRS-based carrier frequency offset compensation also removes the Doppler shift of a dominant line-of-sight path, invalidating the LMMSE correlation model and costing 0.84 dB, which can produce illusory gains for learned receivers. Code, configurations and results: https://github.com/Ewwftyy/neural-receiver-5g-nr
items.title: Training Coverage, Not Architecture, Decides When Learned 5G NR Receivers Help

items.summary: Аннотация. В статье проанализированы публикации газеты «Слава Севастополя» как исторического источника, позволяющего изучить реализацию антиалкогольной кампании 1985–1990 гг. в Севастополе. Рассмотрены основные типы материалов, опубликованных на страницах издания: официальные постановления и отклики, репортажи об административных мерах, пропаганда безалкогольной обрядности, критические статьи о работе общества трезвости, материалы о негативных последствиях кампании, а также публикации о ситуации в виноградарстве и торговле. Сделан вывод, что газета является значимым источником при исследовании кампании, поскольку она не только транслировала официальную пропаганду, но и отражала реальные противоречия и провалы, что позволяет реконструировать как официальную картину, так и повседневные практики населения.   Abstract. The article analyzes publications of the newspaper «Glory of Sevastopol» as a historical source that allows studying the implementation of the anti-alcohol campaign of 1985–1990 in Sevastopol. The main types of materials published in the newspaper are examined: official resolutions and responses, reports on administrative measures, propaganda of non-alcoholic rituals, critical articles on the work of the sobriety society, materials on the negative consequences of the campaign, as well as publications on the situation in viticulture and trade. It is concluded that the newspaper is a significant source for studying the campaign, since it not only conveyed official propaganda but also reflected real contradictions and failures, which makes it possible to reconstruct both the official picture and the everyday practices of the population.

items.summary: This paper argues that river deltas and arterial trees, though studied in separate fields, share a common mathematical architecture. Using side-by-side images as a Rosetta stone, it treats their resemblance as a diagnostic clue rather than a metaphor. Both are described as rooted, planar, directed, space-filling trees with a single inlet, repeated branching, and many terminal outlets. At every internal junction, flow is conserved. Both exhibit hierarchical scaling and self-similarity. The central contribution is a common variational template. If a branching network minimizes a separable cost combining transport dissipation and maintenance or volume cost, then optimal branch sizes at each junction obey a power-law relation. The exponent depends on the physics: viscous laminar flow yields Murray's law for blood vessels, while Manning-style open-channel flow yields a different, testable river scaling. Thus the template does not prove identity; it shows that one abstract optimization structure can generate known biological scaling and a conditional geophysical prediction. The paper then asks why such similarity exists. It offers conjectures: convergent optimization, constructal law, diffusion-limited aggregation, resource constraints, robustness, and a universal attractor. It states falsification tests: scaling exponents and graph metrics should not be random after conditioning on constraints, and diagnostics should transfer across domains. A second theoretical part connects the networks to thin and thick chaos. It defines a diagnostic tuple and proves transport-graph invariance: if two transport graphs are isomorphic in the relevant sense, preserving coherent and failure regions and the ordering of edge weights, then thin, transitional, and thick classifications transfer. This supports cross-domain diagnostics for flood forecasting and cardiovascular risk, for example, tracking failure pathways. The paper is careful about limits. Rivers and arteries differ physically in fluid, compliance, timescale, and dynamics. The claim is structural and mathematical, not physical identity. The unity is a shared abstract architecture, not sameness.
items.title: One Tree, Two Fluids: Convergent Mathematical Architecture of River Deltas and Arterial Trees

items.summary: International Environmental Law stands at a crossroad, where its basic ideas and principles are massively coming at odds with the depth and demand of universal environmental catastrophe. Greatly based upon notions of state control, assent, and fragmented international agreement, the discipline has failed to respond to massive environmental degradation and biodiversity failure. The formation of the scientific notion of the ecological boundaries and limits has elevated the constraint by introducing a bunch of environmental thresholds and limits within which the humankind can remain secure. Developed by the Stockholm Resilience Centre, this framework uncovers crucial biodiversity dynamics like the massive ecological destruction, ecological threshold, poor land usage and change, and bio-geochemical cycles and hence introduces a novice standard beyond which the irreparable environmental damage sharply increases and spikes. While this model has gained impeccable speed and admiration among scientific and policy stakeholders, its ethical interpretation and application for international law remains questionable. This paper argues that adopting environmental limits within the scope and ambit of international environmental law calls for a thorough transformation from fragmented governance towards an obligatory structure of earth system governance.
items.title: Planetary Boundaries And International Environmental Law: Towards Earth System Governance

items.summary: Let a consumer trust its cache instead of re-fetching it trust_cached_entries (default False ) serves a cache entry as it is on disk: no staleness re-fetch, and no full-text retry. Staleness re-fetching suits a cache the tool owns and can rebuild. For a cache that is committed to a repository and reviewed it inverts — the re-fetch becomes the risk rather than the repair. Three failures reported downstream were the same re-fetch seen from different angles: an unstamped full_text_html entry withheld, pointing at a repair route that cannot be reached ( dismech#12672 ) a fetch returning PMC's bot-check page on an HTTP 200, its <title> then compared against the curated title ( dismech#12867 ) a re-fetch shortening 64 bodies and breaking snippets that had verified, in a pull request about something else ( dismech#12879 ) Setting the flag removes the fetch, so there is no window in which any of them can happen. The default is unchanged, so caches still migrate for consumers that want that. The trade is explicit: an imperfect cached entry stays imperfect. That is a content problem to fix deliberately — cache reference --force still rebuilds one on purpose — rather than something re-litigated on every validation run. Also in this release Review follow-ups from #94: a test for the refused-overwrite path that consumers actually take (the previous tests only covered _stale_fallback ), a stale-HTML warning that no longer advises a retry that cannot succeed for a PMC-only article, find_pmc_article_body made public since two modules share it, and a note that PMC_ARTICLE_BODY_CLASSES is ordered by priority. items.summary: Pipeline and derived matrices for a three-domain calibration of cross-study agreement among public transcriptomic signatures. The analysis covers 19 human datasets: peripheral blood in COVID-19 (10 datasets), peripheral blood in sepsis (5), and aortic wall in dissection or aneurysm (4). This gives 61 pairwise signature comparisons. Headline results. Median pairwise Jaccard overlap was 0.014, 0.072 and 0.023 across the three domains. Observed overlap was 5.6, 10.2 and 6.5 times the expectation for random gene sets of the same size, with 47 of 61 pairs significant after FDR correction. Consensus across ten COVID-19 blood datasets retained two genes from a union of 4,225, and relaxing agreement to 20 per cent retained 717. Simulations with a known shared 250-gene signature hold at 250 for every k and converge after two datasets, so the failure is unstable detection rather than sample size. The release contains a size-aware concordance measure, a permutation null, consensus analysis across datasets, ground-truth simulations in shared-signal and private-signal regimes, and an offline reproduction bundle. No expression matrices are redistributed; all 19 datasets are public and cited by accession in the paper.
items.title: Size-aware cross-dataset concordance of public transcriptomic signatures

items.summary: Predicted protein structures are now abundant but imperfect, and low per-residue confidence (pLDDT) is widely taken to mark regions worth refining. Before building a refiner, we test that premise directly: does low pLDDT actually predict AlphaFold contact error? Using a homology-controlled benchmark of matched AlphaFold-model (AFDB) inputs and experimental (PDB) targets, we compare AlphaFold and experimental contacts for every long-range residue pair and relate per-pair error to pLDDT. Across all 231 benchmark chains (4,208,603 long-range pairs; the effective sample is 231 chains, since pairs are pseudo-replicated within proteins), AlphaFold’s long-range contact calls are almost all correct — but this is expected, since most long-range pairs are non-contacts, so we focus on the contact-relevant errors. The per-pair contact-error rate is 0.0036 (95% bootstrap CI over chains 0.0033–0.0040), decomposed into false-positive contacts (asserted but absent) and missed real contacts. Low pLDDT is associated with elevated contact error (0.0089 below pLDDT 70 versus 0.0024 above, a 3.70× enrichment, 95% CI 3.3–4.1), but predicts it only weakly: the discrimination AUC of pLDDT as a contact-error score is 0.672 (95% CI 0.65–0.69), the best Youden threshold is near pLDDT 81 and the best F1 threshold near pLDDT 52, and pLDDT < 70 captures only 46% of all contact errors at sub-percent precision. False-positive (44%) and false-negative (56%) errors have different pLDDT profiles. Sequence/evolutionary information (ESM-2 contact probabilities) identifies these errors partially (AUC 0.61–0.63 for false positives, 0.66–0.86 for missed contacts), and low-confidence pairs that sit near a high-confidence anchor have a lower error rate (0.0074 versus 0.0090), suggesting anchor-based correction is a direction worth pursuing. Consistent with the weak localization of error, on a common subset of chains a hybrid Transformer–geometric refiner selected on validation precision cannot be distinguished from a copy-input baseline that trusts the AlphaFold structure (paired bootstrap over chains does not exclude zero difference). The practical conclusion is that on high-quality AlphaFold inputs there is little contact error to recover and pLDDT does not localize it well; useful refinement will need error-specific, evolutionarily grounded signal and may exploit high-confidence anchors. We release the benchmark, the characterization pipeline, and the code.
items.title: AlphaFold Contact Errors and pLDDT — Homology-Controlled Benchmark and Characterization

items.summary: This dataset provides the nationally consistent, footprint-level classification of residential building subtypes across the United States. It contains over 140 million building footprints classified into four distinct structural residential categories:  Single-Family Homes (SFHs), Townhouses (including duplexes), Apartments, and Mobile Homes .    The dataset is organized geographically and stored as individual, high-performance GeoPackage ( .gpkg ) files for each of the 50 U.S. states and the District of Columbia .   Data Schema (Attribute Fields) Each state-level GeoPackage contains the following standardized attribute columns:   geometry (Polygon) : The spatial boundary (polygon) of the building footprint. Res_type (Integer) : The classified residential structural subtype code: 1 = Single-Family Home (SFH) 2 = Townhouse (explicitly includes laterally attached row houses and semi-detached duplexes) 3 = Apartment 4 = Mobile Home height (Double) : The estimated physical height of the building in meters. Baseline heights are obtained from Microsoft Global ML footprints, with a minimum threshold of 4.2 m enforced (representing a typical one-story structure) and missing values imputed using local tract-level medians. type (String) : Building type tags from OSM building footprint (Limited coverage and varies by region).   Methodology and Classification Workflow The residential classifications were achieved using a novel, scalable hierarchical spatial workflow that integrates geometric building footprints with high-confidence administrative and demographic auxiliary data:   Multi-Source Footprint Integration: Geometry was compiled by merging Microsoft US Building Footprints, Microsoft Global ML Building Footprints, and OpenStreetMap (OSM) geometries. Non-residential structures were purged during preprocessing using OSM land-use layers and manual reclassification of OSM building tags. Mobile Home Identification: Candidate footprints located within spatial buffers around documented mobile home parks were classified using state-specific Random Forest (RF) models trained on footprint geometry (area, aspect ratio, rectangularity, and local density). High-confidence "seeds" were subsequently expanded using context-aware spatial promotion rules. Single-Family Home (SFH) Calibration: High-confidence SFHs were initially mapped using administrative address attributes. To prevent over- or under-counting, a size-ranked rule-based spatial promotion algorithm was implemented to sequentially classify candidate footprints until the counts aligned with rigorous state-level housing stock benchmarks derived from the American Community Survey (ACS) 5-year estimates. Townhouse and Apartment Discrimination: The remaining unclassified structures were categorized using a sequential, rule-based physical geometry and address-point pattern-recognition workflow. Duplexes and linear townhouses were distinguished from multi-family apartment blocks by evaluating physical constraints (convexity, height, and structural width) paired with the spatial density and linear alignment of internal address points from the National Address Database (NAD) . Spatial Context Completion: A final, iterative morphological distance-matching algorithm resolved any remaining unclassified structures based on local neighborhood class composition and physical architectural similarities (height, area, and aspect ratio).
items.title: Nationwide Footprint-Level Classification of Residential Building Subtypes for the United States

items.summary: Artifact accompanying a manuscript under double-blind review . Author information is withheld until publication; a later version of this record will carry it, and the concept DOI is stable across versions. What this is. When two unlabelled subgroups of documents are compared by embedding similarity across languages, countries, corpora or periods, and the difference is read as evidence about those sources, no accuracy figure certifies that reading. within_language_baseline.py supplies the missing baseline: it measures the same subgroup contrast inside a single source, where no across-source relation can enter, and reports the residual with a bootstrap interval and an equivalence verdict against a margin declared in advance. The tool has no dependency on the accompanying study and runs on any corpus with three columns ( text , group , source ). It carries its own injection tests ( --selftest ). The bootstrap resamples documents rather than pairs and excludes duplicate draws of the same document from within-source pairs. The model contrasts bottom-up, mixed, and top-down organizational scenarios while incorporating household production, residential mobility, demographic fission, cooperation, surplus transfer, soil degradation and recovery, ecological forcing, and cumulative landscape investment. Global sensitivity analysis additionally evaluates 16 parameters across 180 Latin hypercube sets. The repository provides the R workflow used for data preparation, simulation, validation, sensitivity analysis, figure generation, and manuscript tables, supporting transparent replication, methodological evaluation, comparative reuse in archaeological modeling, and facilitating critical assessment of alternative mechanisms underlying long-term settlement and socio-ecological change patterns.

items.summary: Background: Traditional post-marketing drug monitoring framework metrics rely heavily upon passive, spontaneous clinical case notification configurations. These configurations systematically suffer from extensive reporting lag phases and a massive underreporting of actual consumer adverse drug reactions (ADRs). With the explosive expansion of global digital platforms, modern patient networks frequently document raw, unformatted clinical complaints online long before consulting a healthcare practitioner. Objective: This core research constructs, validates, and evaluates an enterprise cloud architecture prototype termed "Shreyas SmartPV Mobile" to automate case intake pipelines, deploy cognitive semantic extractors, map raw text onto official MedDRA hierarchies, and execute immediate regulatory eligibility checks. Methodology: A multi-layered low-code pipeline structure was engineered using Glide Apps and Softr for responsive frontend client interface extraction, Airtable as the primary secure relational cloud database storage, and Make.com as the background workflow synchronization integration orchestrator. Data streams are processed via a cognitive node driven by the Google Gemini Large Language Model (LLM) framework running specific clinical validation rules, multi-stage Named Entity Recognition (NER), and automated token dictionaries to extract suspect therapeutic drug classes cleanly from descriptive toxicological events. Results: Extensive experimental validation using standard chemical benchmark metrics (including Paracetamol, Aspirin, and Ibuprofen scenarios) verified 100% precision in parsing unstructured digital narratives, mapping baseline complaints to standard MedDRA Preferred Terms (PT) (e.g., matching 'red rashes on skin' to Erythematous Rash), and computing immediate validation states (Report Valid? = True) based on strict international safety compliance requirements. The system recorded an average automated triage execution velocity of less than 3.9 seconds per array. Conclusion: The validated automation workflow confirms that cloud-native cognitive processing pipelines cut manual data entry fatigue, optimize processing costs, and maximize patient-reported signal capture. This technical transition shifts drug safety management from passive tracking arrays into dynamic, real-time digital active safety listening ecosystems.

items.summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/22983291 . General assessment This manuscript addresses an important and underappreciated problem in computational chemistry and molecular machine learning: apparent differences in predictive performance can arise from benchmark construction and target definition rather than from intrinsic superiority of one modelling approach over another. The distinction between literature-reported absorption maxima and calculated vertical excitation energies is scientifically important, and the emphasis on genuinely external validation is a clear strength of the work. However, I find the central conclusion stronger than the evidence presently described appears to support. The results convincingly show that model performance changes substantially across datasets and label conventions. They do not yet demonstrate that label definition, rather than model capability, is the principal cause of the apparent machine-learning advantage over TD-DFT. Several factors change simultaneously across the comparisons presented in the manuscript, including chemical domain, dataset provenance, transition assignment, computational protocol, sample size, and the nature of the machine-learning representation. These factors make it difficult to isolate label definition as the causal explanation. The manuscript raises a valuable methodological concern, but the title and several conclusions should either be moderated or supported by additional controlled analyses. Major comments 1. The title makes a stronger causal claim than the study design appears to establish The title states that benchmark label definition, "not model capability," explains the machine-learning advantage over TD-DFT. This is a strong exclusionary claim. The results show that the apparent ranking between a Gaussian-process model and quantum-chemical calculations changes between evaluation datasets. However, label definition is not the only property that changes between these datasets. Their chemical composition, source literature, distribution of chromophores, spectral range, experimental conditions, and possibly computational protocols also differ. Therefore, demonstrating that a GP performs differently on a dataset with transition-specific labels does not by itself establish that label definition is the cause of the difference. A substantially stronger test would use the same set of molecules with two alternative target definitions—for example, a literature-reported overall λmax and an independently assigned transition-specific λmax—and evaluate both methods against both labels. A paired analysis of this type would isolate label definition while holding molecular distribution constant. Unless such a controlled analysis is provided, I suggest moderating the central conclusion to state that label definition and dataset provenance are important contributors to the reported ML advantage rather than demonstrating that they fully explain it. 2. One Gaussian-process model cannot represent "machine-learning capability" generally The machine-learning side of the comparison is represented by a Gaussian process using 256-bit Morgan fingerprints. This is a relatively specific and comparatively simple model representation. The conclusions therefore apply directly to this GP/fingerprint model, but not necessarily to molecular machine learning more broadly. Modern λmax prediction methods may use larger fingerprints, graph neural networks, message-passing architectures, pretrained molecular representations, three-dimensional information, explicit solvent descriptors, or quantum-chemical features. Such models may respond differently to both chemical and label distribution shifts. items.summary: Conventional black-box predictive models consistently exhaust the limited memory boundaries of industrial edge microcontrollers. Massive parameter footprints and opaque decision pathways render standard neural networks highly vulnerable to out-of-distribution catastrophic failures. The proposed physics-informed symbolic artificial intelligence architecture formulates transparent degradation equations tailored directly to individual hardware characteristics. An autonomous generator fuses fundamental electrical constraints with a localized polynomial expansion to produce extreme low-dimensional operational logic. Empirical evaluations utilizing the NASA Ames repository demonstrate the absolute elimination of cross-run extrapolation errors. The customized equations require a strict maximum footprint of 140 Bytes and execute at a constant O(1) inference complexity. The explicit physical formulation reduces total execution energy consumption by a factor of 2.8 compared to baseline multi-layer perceptrons, while maintaining a 0.9994 accuracy score under severe data scarcity. Synthetic noise injection tests confirm supreme operational resilience against severe sensor distortions. Absolute white-box interpretability provides field engineers with the direct capability to audit the precise prognostic logic prior to chip deployment. The decentralized deployment of deterministic diagnostic intelligence establishes a highly robust foundation for sustainable smart manufacturing ecosystems.
items.title: Physics-Informed Symbolic AI: An Explainable Edge-Native Framework for Industrial Prognostics

items.summary: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-mounted base sta tions and 5G New Radio Integrated Access and Backhaul (NR IAB) can provide flexible wireless coverage in temporary, remote, and mission-critical scenarios. In UAV-assisted NR-IAB networks, UAV mobility affects both the User Equipment (UE) access link and the donor-facing wireless backhaul, making packet-level evaluation necessary for understanding end-to-end performance. This paper presents an ns-3/5G-LENA framework for evaluating communication-aware UAV mobility control in an Evolved Packet Core (EPC)-aware NR-IAB topology. A CoCo-inspired mean field controller is adapted as the baseline, and a Quality-Of Service (QoS)-aware extension is introduced to include previous interval packet delivery and delay in the action-selection process. Factorial sweeps and targeted experiments are used to study controller behavior under different geometries, UE speeds, IAB counts, QoS weights, and traffic profiles. Overall, the results show that swarm-level improvements in coverage and backhaul quality do not necessarily guarantee better packet delivery or delay performance, while the marginal gains of the proposed QoS aware extension compared to the baseline mean-field controller, highlight the difficulty of translating packet-level feedback into effective UAV-IAB mobility decisions.
tags: 5G NR, Integrated Access and Backhaul, UAV networks, UAV-IAB, swarm mobility control, CoCo, QoS-aware control, ns-3, 5G-LENA
items.title: Bridging 5G-IAB Networking and Swarm Intelligence: Evaluating Distributed UAV Coordination Under Mission-Critical Communication Constraints

items.summary: emgteach is an open-source Python package that provides a unified PySide6 desktop application for real-time acquisition, offline analysis and maximum voluntary contraction (MVC) normalisation of surface electromyography (sEMG) signals. It is designed for hands-on biopotential acquisition in undergraduate physiology teaching laboratories, and is meant to be set up by instructors with different levels of technical background and used directly by students during a practical session. The application is hardware-agnostic through a common AcquisitionDevice interface and ships with two interchangeable low-cost backends: BITalino (revolution) over Bluetooth, and an Arduino RedBoard Plus + MyoWare 2.0 over USB serial (open firmware included). A single setting switches between them. Main features: Three-tab GUI (Acquisition, Analysis, MVC normalisation) wrapping a reusable, Qt-free analytic core. Bilingual interface (English / Spanish) with automatic start-up language detection and an in-app language switch. Two-channel acquisition (e.g. agonist/antagonist) with a stacked two-channel live view. Automatic contraction-onset detection (baseline + k·SD threshold) stored as EDF+ annotations. Muscle-load analysis (Jonsson APDF): static (P10), median (P50) and peak (P90) %MVC levels, both offline and as a live monitor with warning/danger zones. One-click PDF session and MVC/muscle-load reports. Reliable EDF+ output using a buffered-write pattern that avoids a silent file-corruption artefact during continuous streaming. Assisted selection of significant fragments, with an editable fragment editor (detection parameters and envelope-filter cut-offs) applied to the analysis. CSV export of results and a live signal-quality check during recording. Classroom mode: a read-only live dashboard served over the local network so students follow the session on their phone/tablet browser (no install), with a per-session access code so the follower link only works while the broadcast is running. Kinematics via the BITalino accelerometer (v2.0.0): a movement-versus-EMG analysis panel, a guided force-velocity acquisition wizard (an MVC maximum followed by cued quick lifts, each auto-marked with its load), and a force-velocity study that turns one recording into the load-velocity, Hill force-velocity, power and recruitment curves. Since v3.0.0 the accelerometer's input is a stated convention (muscle on A1, accelerometer on A2) rather than a selectable channel. Configuration by practical (v3.0.0): three practicals — one muscle, agonist/antagonist and muscle kinematics — fix the channel count, the accelerometer and what each tab offers, replacing the settings that were previously chosen one at a time. The session as a single file with its phases marked inside it (v3.0.0): warm-up, calibration repetitions, preparation and recording, so the maximum voluntary contraction every percentage is measured against travels with the signal, and a derived (tuned) recording carries the decisions taken on screen. Teaching layer (v3.0.0): a guided tour over the interface, contextual help on every box, one analysis row per contraction with its electromechanical delay, and an agonist/antagonist co-activation index (Falconer-Winter) computed per marked phase in %MVC. Handling at the laboratory bench (v3.1.0): the fragment editor as a three-step procedure that counts the marked contractions against the protocol and lets each be kept, dropped, split or dragged, with the detection sensitivity set per practical and recorded in the report and the CSV; a single running instance with a start-up splash; pictures of the electrode placement and the calibration in the guided tour; and a printable sheet for each station of the agonist/antagonist practical. Patch 3.1.1: the co-activation of a named window is read on the uncut recording, with each muscle's resting level taken from the whole recording phase, so choosing fragments no longer measures the antagonist against a rest taken from a signal
items.title: emgteach: an open-source teaching platform for surface electromyography

items.summary: A systematic framework for quantum algorithm development covering 20 scientific problem domains with standardized maturity gates, automated validation, resource estimation pipelines, and Azure Quantum integration. Problems are held to explicit maturity gates rather than assumed to pass them: 9 problems are at Stage C, 8 remain at Stage B, and 3 have reached Stage D. All 20 have real Azure Quantum Resource Estimator profiles (1,746 to 754,715 physical qubits), and all 20 calibration ensembles carry valid statistics bound to hashes of the Q# sources they ran. No problem currently demonstrates quantum advantage on available hardware, and 11 of the 20 were downgraded on I/O bottlenecks, quadratic-only speedups or no proven speedup. Implements 10 algorithm families (VQE, QAOA, Grover, HHL, Shor, amplitude estimation, swap test, QEC, quantum walk, Trotter simulation) using the modern Microsoft QDK (qsharp 1.31.0, no .NET dependency); the hardware kernels of the five VQE problems have since been replaced by quantum phase estimation. Also includes a deployed evaluation service that routes a natural-language problem description to one of four verdicts using a deterministic rule set rather than model judgement, a paper classifier measured for over-claim rate against a labelled corpus, and generated Q# that is compiled and resource-estimated before it is reported. Includes cross-problem comparison dashboard, per-problem detail pages with charts, and embedded README documentation.
items.title: Quantum Grand Challenges: Systematic Quantum Algorithm Development Across 20 Application Domains

items.summary: A thirteen-chapter monograph on geometric and analytic structures that recur in quantum gravity. The chapters range from functional realizations of matrices and tensors to emergent spacetime. Each chapter separates proved results from conjectures and heuristic proposals, and states that status explicitly. Part I (Ch. 1–2) studies functional realizations of matrices and tensors and geometric flows on matrix, tensor and graphon spaces. Part II (Ch. 3–6) covers: - the analytic continuation of Pascal's simplex; - Beta-kernel operators; - interdimensional transforms; - analysis on Sierpiński simplices. Proved results in Part II include: - the asymptotics of continuous multinomial integrals; - an expansion of the continuous row entropy via the Barnes G-function; - an inversion formula for the Radon–Beta transform. Part III (Ch. 7–10) develops the L∞ minimax extrinsic-curvature problem for submanifolds and curves in obstacle domains. Its proved results include: - existence for curves; - a contact principle; - sharp U-turn bounds in Euclidean and constant-curvature spaces; - finiteness of homotopy classes under a length bound. Part III also treats applications to ADM slicings and relativistic trajectories. It shows the limits of transferring the problem to information geometry. Part IV (Ch. 11–12) reviews established links between entanglement, tensor networks and gravity, with sources (linearized Einstein equations from the entanglement first law, min-cut bounds, the loop-quantum-gravity area spectrum). It formulates the open questions as conjectures. Part V (Ch. 13) is an order-of-magnitude assessment. It concludes that Planck-suppressed signatures of the two-scale spectral-dimension model lie far below current and planned sensitivities. The Lean 4 files in the companion repository are a naming skeleton and do not verify the mathematics. LaTeX sources, numerical checks, audit records and the register of findings are in the repository: https://github.com/reinaldomsilvafilho-netizen/quantum-gravity-lean4
items.title: Geometry, Tensors, and Quantum Gravity
